wins.text: Daily sales rate grew 5% YoY in Q1 2025, the strongest DSR since Q2 2023, driven by self-help execution and contract signings
National, regional and government contract count grew at a double-digit rate for 12 consecutive months; healthy pace and mix of signings continued in Q1 2025
FMI device count reached ~130,000 across 25 countries, up 12.5% YoY; digital footprint expanded to 61% of total sales vs. 59% a year ago
On-site customer sites (>$50K/month) grew 7% YoY; safety sales grew nearly 10% in March driven by FMI execution
Dividend increased from $0.43 to $0.44/quarter, putting the company on track to pay over $1 billion in regular dividends for the first time in 2025

risks.text: Operating margin declined 50 bps YoY to 20.1% in Q1 2025; gross margin fell 40 bps to 45.1% due to product/customer mix, higher third-party freight costs, and elevated hub vehicle lease costs

Significant tariff exposure: 145% total duty on non-steel China imports and 25% Section 232 on steel/derivative products (including fasteners globally); management acknowledged 'there is no silver bullet' and no way to cushion 145% tariffs
End market demand remains sluggish; customer tone shifted from steady post-election improvement to plateauing as trade policy created caution; no meaningful pre-buying observed

Inventory up 11.9% YoY as company accelerated purchases ahead of tariffs; operating cash conversion was only 88% of net income, below typical Q1 levels; inventory growth may remain elevated throughout 2025

Fastener supply chain heavily concentrated in Asia with no scale North American manufacturing alternative; company found no viable domestic/Mexico substitute to satisfy fastener sourcing needs at scale

guidance_items.detail: Pricing actions taken in April expected to contribute 3%-4% price uplift in Q2 2025, with potential to double to 6%-8% in H2 2025 depending on pace and execution
Full-year 2025 capex guided to $265M-$285M, up from $214M in 2024, driven by FMI device spending, IT/digital capabilities, and distribution center outlays (Utah, Atlanta hubs)
Easier gross margin comparisons expected in H2 2025; effectiveness of price-cost management and macro improvement will influence outcome; goal remains to defend gross margin percentage

No formal revenue guidance issued; management expressed limited visibility and shared customers' uncertainty over trade policy impact on 2025 demand, but noted internal momentum and easier comps as tailwinds

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Feasibility and magnitude of 145% China tariff impact on customer contracts and sourcing optionality
Availability of North American/Mexico-based fastener manufacturing as a supply chain alternative
Gross margin outlook update given price-cost dynamics and tariff environment
